name: 01_hidden_bridge
title: A hidden bridge
description: Actual affine points over F7 for y^2=x^3+1 and y^2=x^3+6. The identity O is included in the stated counts. They become isomorphic over F49.

name: 02_finite_curve_points
title: A finite-field curve is a set of points
description: A complete F7 grid for y^2=x^3+1, including an example modular check and the identity point in the total.

name: 03_field_toolbox
title: Extending the coordinate toolbox
description: The field F49 is obtained by adjoining a square root of 3 to F7. It is a field of pairs, not integers modulo 49.

name: 04_explicit_hidden_map
title: A point crossing the hidden bridge
description: An explicit isomorphism from y^2=x^3+1 to y^2=x^3+6 over F49. A base-field point can map to a point with extension-field coordinates.

name: 05_quadratic_square_flip
title: Quadratic twisting flips square choices
description: The complete fiber-by-fiber counts for y^2=x^3+1 and 3v^2=x^3+1 over F7. Each x contributes two points across the two models.

name: 06_coordinate_weight_tree
title: Why 2, 3, 4 and 6 appear
description: The Weierstrass coordinate weights force the generic square-root case and permit fourth or sixth roots when a coefficient vanishes. Cubic twists are a subfamily of sextic twists.

name: 07_symmetry_groups
title: More symmetry permits more twists
description: Symbolic diagrams of the origin-preserving geometric automorphism groups C2, C4 and C6. These polygons are not drawings of the curves.

name: 08_cubic_family
title: The cubic-twist triangle
description: The three cubic twists of y^2=x^3+1 over F7 have coefficients 1, 2 and 4, and point counts 12, 9 and 3. Arrows represent multiplication of B by 2, a square, with a cube-root coordinate change.

name: 09_quartic_family
title: The quartic-twist family
description: The four quartic twist classes over F13 of y^2=x^3+x, with coefficients 1,2,4,8 and exact extension degrees 1,4,2,4.

name: 10_sextic_family_wheel
title: All six sextic-twist classes
description: Six F7-isomorphism classes with j=0. Each node gives B, the actual point count, and the minimal isomorphism-extension degree relative to B=1. Dashed purple lines identify its cubic subfamily.

name: 11_field_changes_class_count
title: The field changes the number of twists
description: For j=0 and characteristic greater than 3, the sextic classes are multiplicative cosets modulo sixth powers. This gives six classes over F7 and two over F5.

name: 12_frobenius_visibility
title: Frobenius is the visibility test
description: Base-field rational points are fixed by Frobenius. Under a quadratic untwist, rational points on the twist correspond to anti-fixed points pi(P)=-P, which are fixed by pi squared. Two-torsion can satisfy both conditions.

name: 13_twist_security
title: Why the quadratic-twist order matters
description: A Montgomery single-coordinate ladder can process inputs associated with either the curve or its quadratic twist. Each group needs the order properties required by the protocol. A nonzero right-hand side is assumed in the branch labels.

name: 14_pairing_field_tower
title: A sextic twist makes pairing points cheaper
description: BLS12-381 represents G2 on its M-type sextic twist over Fp2. The untwist embeds the selected subgroup in E(Fp12). Pairing values live in a multiplicative subgroup of Fp12, a different object from elliptic-curve points.
